items.q: Are AQUASKY pressure tanks marked "CE"?

items.q: What is NSF 61?

a.p: NSF/ANSI 61 is a North American health effects standard for materials and components in contact with drinking water. It ensures products do not leach harmful contaminants into potable water systems. Select AQUASKY potable pressure tank series are fully certified to NSF/ANSI 61 and NSF/ANSI 58.

items.q: Can the pre-charge pressure of AQUASKY pressure tanks be modified?

a.p: **Yes, the pre-charge pressure of AQUASKY pressure tanks can be adjusted** between 0.5 bar (7 psi) and 3.5 bar (50 psi) when the tank is completely empty of water. To ensure system safety and proper calibration, adjustments should be performed by a qualified technician.

items.q: What information is required and how do you size AQUASKY pressure tanks?

You can calculate the exact tank capacity using our online [**AQUASKY Selection Tool**]({selTools}) or contact our technical team for custom sizing support.

items.q: How does the pressure switch control the pump and tank?

a.p: **The pressure switch regulates water system pressure by monitoring the pressure inside the tank and automatically cycling the pump on and off.** When system pressure drops to the preset cut-in threshold, the switch activates the pump to refill the tank; once pressure reaches the cut-out limit, it shuts the pump off.

items.q: What are usual cut-ins and cut-outs?

a.p: **The most common residential pressure switch settings are 30/50 psi and 40/60 psi, maintaining a standard 20 psi differential.** For example, in a 30/50 psi system, the pump starts (cut-in) when pressure drops to 30 psi and stops (cut-out) at 50 psi, with the pressure tank typically pre-charged 2 psi below the cut-in pressure.

items.q: What is the usual pre-charge for a pressure tank?

a.p: **For potable water booster systems, the tank pre-charge should be set 2 psi (0.14 bar) below the pump cut-in pressure**—typically 28 psi for a 30/50 psi switch. For closed-loop heating expansion systems, pre-charge matches the system's cold static fill pressure. All AQUASKY pressure tanks are factory pre-charged with nitrogen (N₂) and tested before shipment.

items.q: In your QC process, what are the standards for pressure cycle testing?

items.q: Why choose a diaphragm pressure tank?

a.p: **A diaphragm tank permanently separates the pressurized nitrogen (N₂) cushion from the water, preventing waterlogging, internal corrosion, and pressure loss.** Compared to standard air-over-water tanks, AQUASKY diaphragm pressure tanks maintain consistent system pressure, reduce pump short-cycling, and feature food-grade diaphragms with **NSF/ANSI 61** certified potable series available.

items.q: Why use nitrogen (N₂) for pre-charging?

a.p: **Nitrogen (N₂) permeates diaphragm rubber much slower than oxygen and remains highly stable across temperature fluctuations.** Compared to compressed air, factory pre-charging with pure, dry nitrogen prevents internal oxidation, maintains consistent pre-charge pressure, and significantly reduces routine maintenance throughout the AQUASKY tank's service life.

items.q: How can you check if the internal diaphragm of a pressure tank is broken?

a.p: You can quickly test whether an AQUASKY pressure tank's internal diaphragm is intact by depressing the gas valve core on top of the tank:

ul: **If nitrogen or air hisses out:** The internal butyl diaphragm is intact. Simply drain the water from the system and restore the tank's pre-charge pressure to **2 psi below** your pump cut-in setting.
**If water sprays or drips out:** The diaphragm has ruptured and water has entered the gas chamber. The pressure tank must be replaced immediately to prevent pump short-cycling and system damage.

items.q: How can I prevent pressure tank malfunctions and maximize product lifespan?

a.p: Follow the technical label and official AQUASKY installation manual, and observe these essential maintenance practices:

ul: **Proper Sizing & Pre-Charge:** Select the correct tank volume and inspect/restore the pre-charge pressure annually.
**Pressure & Surge Protection:** Prevent excessive overpressure and water hammer within the system.
**Electrical Grounding:** Ensure proper system grounding to prevent galvanic corrosion.
**Environmental Protection:** Install in a dry, well-ventilated location to avoid condensation, freezing, and external rust.
**Fluid Compatibility:** Monitor the pH of glycol solutions and never mix different antifreeze agents.
